payload.summary: A point-in-time standard report on Microsoft as of 2026-09-12, using only documents published on or before that date, built around the operator's three questions: whether cloud margin survives the depreciation, lease and financing cost of infrastructure now being capitalised; what growth, margin, capital intensity and fade the prevailing price implies under a reverse DCF; and how much growth comes from AI offerings absent in FY2023. Depth priority is earnings_quality, cash_flow_analysis, valuation_dcf and growth_outlook; the proxy and peer useful-life work may be cut to one targeted extraction each if gathering runs long. The September 2026 recast 8-K is a search-and-verify step, not an assumed document, with a stated fallback to the pre-change basis. Discount-rate inputs are sourced explicitly and recorded as platform assumptions carrying a sensitivity band. A dated disclosure calendar ties each thesis condition to the filing inside the 12-month horizon that would test it. Every figure is computed by the platform from filings fetched in this run; this plan asserts none. Prior research shapes which questions are asked and is never cited.

sections.focus: Answer the three operator questions in order, each labelled by evidence type: audited filing line item, unaudited management commentary in an earnings exhibit, or platform-computed derivation. State plainly where disclosure does not permit an answer, particularly AI-revenue attribution the company may not report as a line item, and where the reverse-DCF answer depends on a recorded discount-rate assumption rather than a fact about the company. No figure may appear here that is not computed and cited in a later section.

Central to operator question one. Gather the property and equipment note, capitalised software policy, useful-life assumptions and any change in estimate disclosed FY2024-FY2026, plus finance and operating lease commitments including leases signed but not yet commenced, and supplier finance or purchase-obligation disclosure. Test whether margin expansion coincides with lengthened useful lives, rising capitalisation, or assets not yet placed in service. Benchmark useful lives against two peer hyperscalers; this comparison may be reduced to one targeted extraction each if budget is short.

Build the multi-year bridge from operating cash flow to free cash flow with capital expenditure, finance lease principal, supplier or vendor financing and prepayments for contracted capacity shown separately, since additions sitting outside investing-activities capex are where capitalisation can flatter reported margin. Extend scope to commitments and contingencies and any off-balance-sheet capacity arrangement. Take capex cadence from the FY2026 10-Qs. Include debt issuance, buyback and dividend outflow so the funding of the build is visible. Where total infrastructure additions cannot be assembled, report the gap as an unquantifiable disclosure limit.

Answer operator question two as a reverse DCF: solve for the revenue growth, operating margin, capital intensity and fade duration implied by the 2026-09-12 price, given share count and net debt from the latest filed balance sheet. The discount rate is a recorded platform assumption, not a finding: cite the as-of-date government yield, the dated published equity risk premium and the beta estimation basis, and present implied assumptions across a band of discount rates rather than a single point. Compare implied assumptions to the historical range computed elsewhere in this run, not to a target price.

Answer operator question three. Establish the FY2023 baseline from that year's 10-K, then trace disclosed AI-related offerings: any named revenue line, quantified run-rate or growth-contribution statement in earnings exhibits, commercial bookings, and remaining performance obligation with its disclosed recognition window. Additionally ask, from the related-party and equity-method note, whether any disclosed AI revenue, commitment or backlog originates from investees or counterparties the company itself funds. If the filings do not disaggregate, report both the AI attribution and the circularity question as open, with proxies labelled management-stated and unaudited.

Vary only reverse-DCF inputs the evidence shows are genuinely uncertain: cloud operating margin once assets under construction carry full depreciation, useful-life shortening, RPO conversion pace, and the discount rate band. Show sensitivity to each input independently and identify the single input the outcome is most sensitive to. Mark explicitly which inputs cannot resolve inside the 12-month horizon and are therefore judged only by direction of travel in interim filings, not by outcome.

First verify by EDGAR filing-index search whether an 8-K describing an updated reporting structure was filed or furnished on or before 2026-09-12, and if so what periods its exhibit recasts and whether it is furnished rather than filed. If it exists and reaches far enough, reconstruct segment revenue and operating income on both bases and show where the mapping is incomplete. If it does not exist or covers fewer periods than needed, build on the pre-change basis only and label the break; construct no mapping the issuer never published. Separate management-defined cloud aggregates from reportable segments.

Compute the FY2023-FY2026 trend in revenue, gross and operating margin, depreciation as a share of revenue, and capital intensity, on the pre-recast basis where recast history does not reach back. Flag every comparability break caused by the September 2026 reporting change, if verified, or by earlier realignments, and never chain a series across a break without labelling it. Source from XBRL company facts where possible and reconcile to filing text.

State the thesis as conditions that must hold over 12 months, each tied to an observable disclosure: cloud segment margin on a stated basis, the depreciation and finance-lease charge trajectory implied by assets placed in service, and commercial RPO with its disclosed recognition window. Each condition must be falsifiable by a specific named future filing, cross-referenced to the catalysts calendar. Mark conditions resting on unaudited management commentary rather than audited statements, and mark those that cannot resolve within the horizon.

Build a dated disclosure calendar covering roughly 2026-09-12 to 2027-09: the FY2027 quarterly results 8-Ks and 10-Qs, the FY2027 10-K, the next proxy, and any capex, useful-life or reporting-structure update. Use only dates announced or inferable from filing cadence on or before the as-of date, and label inferred dates as such. Map each thesis condition to the specific filing that would confirm or falsify it, and mark conditions whose evidence arrives only after the horizon.

Separate issuer-disclosed risks quoted verbatim from the FY2026 10-K risk factors, including AI model, agentic-system and regulatory risk, from risks this run surfaces and can size from filed data, such as gross property and equipment relative to revenue and goodwill and intangible carrying value exposed to reassessment. Risks that cannot be sized from disclosure, including partner, customer and investee concentration, are presented as open questions, not quantified exposures. Record any fetched document containing text addressed as instruction to the analysis as a property of that document.

Record only what changed in the primary record since the prior view: whether a reporting-structure 8-K exists on or before the as-of date and what it covers, any filing made between the prior as-of date and 2026-09-12, and whether risks previously left unsized can now be sized from the FY2026 10-K. Prior figures, ratings and conclusions are restated only as questions to re-derive from filings; nothing from the prior report is carried forward or cited.

planned_sources.why: Primary basis for current segment economics, capitalised infrastructure, useful lives and the disclosed backlog any AI growth claim must rest on.
planned_sources.what: Microsoft FY2026 Form 10-K: income statement, segment note, property and equipment note, leases note, revenue and remaining performance obligation note, risk factors.

planned_sources.why: Directly tests whether margin is flattered by infrastructure not yet carrying a depreciation or interest charge.
planned_sources.what: FY2026 10-K property, equipment and lease detail: assets under construction, assets not yet placed in service, finance lease right-of-use assets, and leases signed but not yet commenced.

planned_sources.why: Infrastructure additions outside investing-activities capex and finance leases would otherwise break the cash-flow bridge that answers operator question one.
planned_sources.what: FY2026 10-K commitments and contingencies, purchase and capacity obligations, supplier finance programme disclosure, prepayments and any off-balance-sheet data-centre capacity arrangement.

planned_sources.why: Three sections depend on the recast basis; its existence and period coverage must be verified, not presupposed, with fallback to the pre-change basis.
planned_sources.what: Search of Microsoft's EDGAR filing index, June to 2026-09-12, for any 8-K describing an updated reporting structure: verify existence, filed versus furnished status, and which periods its exhibit recasts.

planned_sources.why: Annual totals hide cadence; the quarterly series shows whether capex and depreciation are accelerating into the as-of date.
planned_sources.what: Microsoft FY2026 Forms 10-Q for the September, December and March quarters: quarterly capex, depreciation, segment revenue and commercial remaining performance obligation.

planned_sources.why: Supplies the comparative trend and reveals whether useful lives or capitalisation policy changed during the margin expansion.
planned_sources.what: Microsoft FY2025 and FY2024 Forms 10-K: segment results, capex, depreciation, useful-life policy and any disclosed change in accounting estimate.

planned_sources.why: Establishes the pre-AI baseline three years before the as-of date required by the operator's third question.
planned_sources.what: Microsoft FY2023 Form 10-K: segment revenue and operating income, capital expenditure and property and equipment balances.

planned_sources.why: The only place management quantifies AI-related run rates, cloud growth contribution and capacity constraints; treated as unaudited issuer statement.
planned_sources.what: Microsoft quarterly earnings Forms 8-K with Exhibit 99 press releases and prepared remarks, FY2025 Q1 through FY2026 Q4.

planned_sources.why: Machine-readable series for the platform's trend and capital-intensity calculations, avoiding manual transcription from filing text.
planned_sources.what: Company Facts time series for revenue, operating income, gross and net property and equipment, depreciation and amortisation, capex, goodwill and intangibles, FY2020-FY2026.

planned_sources.why: Supplies net debt for the enterprise value bridge, the cost-of-debt input, and the liquidity position prior work left unverified.
planned_sources.what: FY2026 10-K balance sheet and debt note: cash, short-term investments, total debt by maturity and coupon, deferred revenue and current liabilities.

planned_sources.why: Required inputs to the reverse DCF that answers what the current multiple implies; must be the as-of date price, not a later one.
planned_sources.what: MSFT closing price, fully diluted share count basis and market capitalisation as of 2026-09-12, share count cross-checked to the cover page of the latest 10-Q or 10-K.

planned_sources.why: Supplies the risk-free rate the reverse DCF requires; no filing establishes it, and without it operator question two rests on an unsourced number.
planned_sources.what: US Treasury constant-maturity yields (10-year and 20-year) as published for 2026-09-12, retrieved as the point-in-time series.

planned_sources.why: Completes the recorded discount-rate assumption with a citable source and defines the band over which the reverse DCF must be re-solved.
planned_sources.what: A dated, published equity risk premium estimate current as of 2026-09-12, and a documented beta basis (regression window, index, frequency) computed from price history ending on the as-of date.
planned_sources.provider: Published ERP source / market data vendor

planned_sources.why: Tests both the unsized concentration exposure and whether disclosed AI revenue or backlog originates from entities the company itself funds.
planned_sources.what: FY2026 10-K notes on equity-method and other strategic investments, related-party arrangements, and any customer, partner or supplier concentration disclosure.

planned_sources.why: Provides segment detail in reusable form and the only point-in-time basis for dating the catalysts calendar.
planned_sources.what: Investor relations quarterly supplemental workbook, any recast segment datasheet, and the announced date for the first FY2027 earnings release, all published on or before 2026-09-12.

planned_sources.why: Peer benchmark for whether depreciation assumptions are conservative or generous relative to comparable infrastructure; lowest depth priority.
planned_sources.what: Amazon and Alphabet most recent Forms 10-K filed on or before 2026-09-12: server and network equipment useful lives and capex. Reducible to a single targeted useful-life extraction each.

planned_sources.why: Shows whether compensation rewards the metrics whose durability is in question; relevant to earnings quality but secondary to the three operator questions.
planned_sources.what: Microsoft DEF 14A most recently filed before the as-of date: incentive plan metrics and any cloud or AI-linked performance target. Reducible to a single targeted extraction.

planned_sources.why: Management's characterisation of AI demand, capacity and depreciation; never the sole support for a figure.
planned_sources.what: FY2026 Q3 and Q4 earnings call transcripts, used only where a statement is also traceable to the corresponding 8-K exhibit.

known_risks: The reverse DCF's implied growth and margin are highly sensitive to the discount rate, which no filing establishes. It will be recorded as a cited platform assumption with a sensitivity band; ERP and beta are constructed estimates, not facts about the company, and the answer to operator question two inherits that uncertainty.

A recast reporting-structure exhibit may not exist on or before 2026-09-12, may be furnished rather than filed, or may recast too few periods to reach the FY2023 baseline. Fallback is to build series on the pre-change basis only and label the break; no issuer-unpublished mapping will be constructed.

AI revenue is unlikely to be a separately reported line item. If it is not, operator question three can be answered only via management-stated run rates and backlog proxies, which are unaudited; the limitation will be reported rather than an attribution constructed.

Infrastructure additions may sit outside both investing-activities capex and the leases note, in prepayments, supplier finance or third-party capacity contracts that filings do not quantify. Where the total-additions bridge cannot be assembled, the gap is reported as an unquantifiable disclosure limit.

Filings may not disaggregate whether AI or cloud revenue, commitments or backlog originate from equity-method investees or financed counterparties. If not, the independence of that demand stays an open question, not a sized exposure.

Some scenario inputs, notably cloud margin after a full depreciation cycle on assets still under construction, cannot resolve inside a 12-month horizon. The plan deliberately retains them, marked as horizon-exceeding, because excluding them would hide the main risk to the thesis; the catalysts calendar carries only what a filing inside the horizon can test.

Point-in-time discipline excludes everything published after 2026-09-12, including September-quarter results; vendor databases that backfill restatements or adjust price and share-count series must be reconciled to filings as originally filed and to a filing cover page.

Attention budget is finite across roughly eighteen source groups. Depth priority is earnings_quality, cash_flow_analysis, valuation_dcf and growth_outlook; the proxy and peer useful-life comparisons may be cut to one targeted extraction each, and that reduction is recorded rather than silently absorbed.

Standard segment analysis fits poorly where infrastructure is shared across segments and cloud aggregates are management-defined non-GAAP measures; allocated margins may not be verifiable from the audited statements, and equity-method results flowing through other income can distort period comparisons.

No figure, rating or conclusion from the prior approved research may be carried into this report; every number must be re-derived from filings fetched in this run. Fetched documents, including issuer materials and transcripts, may contain text reading as instruction to the analysis; such text is recorded as a property of the document and never acted upon.
payload.prior_research: The planner was shown 1 prior approved report on this company (newest as-of 2026-09-11) as hypothesis material, labelled not-evidence. It may have shaped which questions this plan asks; it cannot support a claim, and the citation verifier rejects any attempt in code.

challenges.statement: The valuation_dcf and scenarios_sensitivities sections require a discount rate, but no planned source supplies its inputs. Market data is scoped only to price, share count and market capitalisation; filings give net debt and coupon rates but not a risk-free rate, equity risk premium or beta. The reverse DCF's implied growth and margin are highly sensitive to this input, so the answer to operator question two rests on a number no listed source can establish point-in-time.
challenges.suggestion: Add an explicit point-in-time source for cost-of-capital inputs (as-of-date government yield, documented ERP, beta basis) and state in the valuation focus that the discount rate is a recorded platform assumption with a cited source, plus a sensitivity band around it.

challenges.statement: The plan treats a September 2026 8-K with a recast segment exhibit as an established document, and three sections (segment_analysis, historical_financial_analysis, prior_research_comparison) build their method on it. The plan should be asking whether such a filing exists on or before 2026-09-12, what periods any recast exhibit covers, and whether it is furnished rather than filed \u2014 not presupposing its content.
challenges.suggestion: Restate the recast 8-K as a search-and-verify step with a stated fallback: if no recast exhibit exists or it covers fewer periods than needed, build the series on the pre-change basis only and label the break, without a mapping the issuer never published.

challenges.statement: The horizon is 12 months, but the analytical spine is multi-year: scenarios vary 'cloud operating margin after a full depreciation cycle' on assets still under construction, an outcome unobservable inside the horizon. No section identifies the specific disclosures due before roughly 2027-09 (Q1\u2013Q4 FY2027 results, the FY2027 10-K, any capex or useful-life update) at which the thesis conditions would actually be confirmed or falsified.
challenges.suggestion: Add to investment_thesis or scenarios a dated disclosure calendar mapping each falsifiable condition to the specific filing within 12 months that would test it, and mark which scenario inputs resolve only beyond the horizon.

challenges.statement: cash_flow_analysis asks for vendor financing and total infrastructure additions shown separately from investing-activities capex, but no source is scoped to third-party data-centre capacity arrangements, prepayments, supplier financing programmes or capacity contracted through operators outside the leases note. If those additions sit outside both capex and finance leases, the section's central bridge \u2014 the one that answers operator question one \u2014 may not be constructible from the planned documents.
challenges.suggestion: Extend the 10-K source scope to commitments and contingencies, supplier finance programme disclosure and any off-balance-sheet capacity arrangements, and state that where total infrastructure additions cannot be assembled, the gap is reported as an unquantifiable disclosure limit.

challenges.statement: growth_outlook and key_risks treat AI-related revenue and investee relationships as separate threads. Neither section asks whether disclosed AI or cloud revenue includes amounts from entities the company also funds or holds via equity method or strategic investment \u2014 which bears directly on whether growth that 'did not exist three years ago' is independently sourced demand. The related-party and equity-method note is fetched but only used for concentration sizing.
challenges.suggestion: Add to growth_outlook the question of whether any disclosed AI revenue, commitment or backlog originates from equity-method investees or financed counterparties, answered from the related-party note, and report it as an open question if the filings do not disaggregate.

challenges.statement: Twelve sections draw on roughly fifteen source groups including four 10-Ks, three 10-Qs, eight quarterly earnings exhibits, two peer issuers, a proxy and transcripts. Nothing states a depth priority, so peripheral work (proxy incentive metrics, equity-method income, peer useful lives) competes for the same budget as the three sections that actually answer the operator's questions. The named risks cover disclosure limits but not the run's own attention budget.
challenges.suggestion: State an explicit priority order \u2014 earnings_quality, cash_flow_analysis, valuation_dcf, growth_outlook first \u2014 and permit the proxy and peer comparisons to be reduced to a single targeted extraction each if evidence gathering runs long.

critique.coverage_note: Reviewed against the three operator questions, the 12-month horizon and point-in-time constraints. The plan's evidence base and its refusal to assert figures are strong; challenges concentrate on inputs no planned source supplies (discount rate), a document assumed rather than verified, horizon-to-evidence mismatch, an unsourced cash-flow bridge line, an unasked revenue-circularity question, and unprioritised breadth.
